skill.name: iac-checkov
skill.description: Guides Checkov security scanning for Terraform, Kubernetes, CloudFormation, Dockerfiles, and related infrastructure-as-code workflows.
skill.summary: Scan infrastructure code with Checkov and turn findings into governed CI checks and remediation priorities.
skill.author: AgentSecOps

security_audit.summary: Manual review dismissed 154 static alerts as documentation, fixed-path parsing, exclusions, placeholders, or safe command examples. One unpinned remote-policy example is confirmed, and semantic review found fail-open CI logic, mutable privileged dependencies, and weakened default enforcement. No prompt injection or data-exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: Mutable CI dependencies can change without review.
remediation.suggestion: Pin actions to commit SHAs, containers to digests, and Python packages to reviewed versions. Grant write permissions only to jobs and steps that need them.

remediation.issue: The GitHub security gate can succeed after scanner failure.
remediation.suggestion: Require the report file, preserve scanner errors, and exit nonzero when Checkov fails or expected output is missing.

remediation.issue: Default templates suppress checks and soften enforcement.
remediation.suggestion: Ship strict production defaults. Move exclusions and soft-fail settings into clearly labeled optional profiles with documented approvals.

remediation.issue: Remote external policies are loaded from a mutable source.
remediation.suggestion: Require reviewed policy repositories and immutable revisions before using external-checks-git. Prefer locally vendored checks with integrity verification.

semantic_findings.title: Security Gate Can Pass When Checkov Fails
semantic_findings.description: The GitHub security gate captures the Checkov exit code but never uses it. If no report is created, the file check is skipped and the step reports success.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The script assigns EXIT_CODE after Checkov, only evaluates findings when the report exists, and has no final nonzero exit. The success message is unconditional.

semantic_findings.title: Mutable CI Dependencies Run With Write Permissions
semantic_findings.description: The workflow grants write permissions globally and runs Checkov actions from the mutable master branch. It also installs unpinned packages and uses latest container tags.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The files explicitly use bridgecrewio/checkov-action@master, pip install without a version, and bridgecrew/checkov:latest. Global write permissions increase the impact of dependency compromise.

semantic_findings.title: Default Templates Weaken Scan Enforcement
semantic_findings.description: The main configuration globally skips several security checks, excludes tests and examples, and soft-fails lower severities. The default pre-commit scan also warns without blocking.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: These settings are active defaults in templates intended for project use. They reduce coverage or enforcement unless adopters notice and override them.

content.value_statement: Infrastructure teams need consistent security checks before deployment. This skill guides Checkov scans, policy customization, suppression governance, compliance mapping, and CI integration.
actual_capabilities: Select Checkov commands for Terraform, Kubernetes, CloudFormation, Dockerfiles, Helm, ARM, and secrets scanning.
Configure severity thresholds, output formats, baselines, path exclusions, and scan scopes.
Explain Python and YAML custom policy structures, testing methods, and loading options.
Adapt example GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Jenkins, and pre-commit integrations.
Map selected Checkov findings to CIS, PCI-DSS, HIPAA, SOC 2, NIST, and GDPR references.
limitations: Checkov and its runtime dependencies must be installed or supplied by a CI image.
The skill scans source definitions and does not validate deployed cloud resources.
Compliance mappings support review but do not provide audit certification.
The guide names several scripts and reference files that are not included in this package.

use_cases.title: Add Pre-Merge IaC Scanning
use_cases.description: Create consistent Checkov checks for pull requests and publish readable security results.

use_cases.title: Govern Policies and Exceptions
use_cases.description: Develop custom checks, test policy behavior, and manage justified suppressions with expiration dates.

use_cases.title: Prepare Compliance Evidence
use_cases.description: Relate scan findings to selected frameworks and organize reports for control review.

prompt_templates.title: Run a First Scan
prompt_templates.prompt: Scan my [IaC path] with Checkov for [framework]. Explain installation, command selection, and how to prioritize the results.

prompt_templates.title: Triage Findings
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these Checkov findings: [paste output]. Group them by severity, identify likely false positives, and propose concrete remediation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Build a CI Gate
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Checkov CI gate for [platform] that blocks [severities], publishes [formats], preserves artifacts, and fails when reports are missing.

prompt_templates.title: Design Policy Governance
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a governed Checkov policy program for [organization]. Include custom policy structure, tests, suppression approvals, dependency pinning, baselines, and compliance reporting.

output_examples.input: Review a Terraform scan with one public storage bucket and three missing tag findings.
output: Priority: Treat the public bucket as urgent because it can expose data.
Remediation: Block public access and verify access policies before deployment.
Follow-up: Resolve tag findings through a shared module after the exposure is fixed.

output_examples.input: Design a GitHub pull request gate for critical and high findings.
output: The gate blocks critical and high findings and publishes a SARIF report.
Scanner failures and missing reports fail the job.
Actions, packages, and container images use reviewed immutable versions.

output_examples.input: Assess a request to suppress an encryption finding for a development database.
output: Decision: Require documented non-production scope and synthetic data.
Approval: Assign an owner, expiration date, and security reviewer.
Compensating control: Restrict network access and monitor database activity.

best_practices: Pin Checkov, CI actions, container images, and external policy sources to reviewed immutable versions.
Treat missing reports and scanner errors as gate failures.
Document every suppression with an owner, reason, expiration date, and compensating controls.
anti_patterns: Do not use blanket suppressions or soft-fail settings for production gates.
Do not load unreviewed external Python policies or mutable CI dependencies.
Do not treat Checkov output as compliance certification without validating controls.

faq.question: Does this skill install Checkov automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides installation and integration guidance, but the user or CI environment must install Checkov.

faq.question: Which infrastructure formats are covered?
faq.answer: The guide covers Terraform, Kubernetes, CloudFormation, Dockerfiles, Helm, ARM, and related Checkov frameworks.

faq.question: Can it scan deployed cloud resources?
faq.answer: No. Checkov primarily analyzes infrastructure definitions and plans, not the complete runtime state of deployed resources.

faq.question: Does a passing scan prove compliance?
faq.answer: No. Scan results support evidence collection, but compliance requires broader control design, operation, and audit validation.

faq.question: How should false positives be handled?
faq.answer: Use narrow suppressions with a clear reason, owner, approval, expiration date, and documented compensating controls.

faq.question: Are the bundled CI templates production ready?
faq.answer: No. Review paths, permissions, enforcement behavior, and dependency pins before using any template in production.
